item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 302306
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM PDT Wed Sep 30 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Nolo, located several hundred miles west of Lihue, Hawaii, on
Hurricane Rachel, located within a couple of hundred miles southwest
of Cabo Corrientes, Mexico, and on Tropical Depression Nineteen-E,
located well west-southwest of the Baja California Peninsula.

South of Southern Mexico:
An area of low pressure could form late this weekend or early next
week south of the southern coast of Mexico. Thereafter,
environmental conditions appear favorable for gradual development,
and a tropical depression could form while the system moves slowly
west-northwestward to northwestward.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...60 percent.

$$
Forecaster Gibbs

item.title: Hurricane Rachel Public Advisory Number 15
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM MST Wed Sep 30 2026 
000
WTPZ33 KNHC 302042
TCPEP3
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Rachel Advisory Number  15
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
200 PM MST Wed Sep 30 2026
 
...RACHEL CONTINUES MOVING NORTHWESTWARD...
...NOAA HURRICANE HUNTER AIRCRAFT DATA INDICATES THE STORM IS
GETTING BETTER ORGANIZED...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 PM MST...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...18.8N 108.0W
ABOUT 185 MI...300 KM SW OF CABO CORRIENTES MEXICO
ABOUT 310 MI...495 KM SSE OF CABO SAN LUCAS MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...85 MPH...140 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 315 DEGREES AT 8 MPH...13 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...978 MB...28.88 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches of warnings in effect.
 
Interests in the southern portion of Baja California Sur should
monitor the progress of Rachel.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 PM MST (2100 UTC), the center of Hurricane Rachel was located
near latitude 18.8 North, longitude 108.0 West. Rachel is moving
toward the northwest near 8 mph (13 km/h). A northwestward motion at
a slower forward speed is expected during the next day or two,
followed by a turn toward the west-northwest and west later this
week. On the forecast track, the center of Rachel is expected to
move away from mainland Mexico and pass south of the Baja California
Peninsula through Thursday.
 
Reports from an NOAA Hurricane Hunter aircraft indicate that 
maximum sustained winds are near 85 mph (140 km/h) with higher
gusts.  Rapid strengthening is expected today and tonight, and
Rachel could become a major hurricane within the next day or so.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 35 miles (55 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 150 miles
(240 km).
 
The minimum central pressure based on the NOAA Hurricane Hunter 
aircraft data is 978 mb (28.88 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Rachel can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP3 and WMO header WTPZ43 KNHC.
 
WIND: Gusts to tropical-storm force are possible along portions of
the coast of southwestern Mexico through tonight.
 
RAINFALL: Rachel is expected to produce additional rainfall totals 
of 2 to 4 inches, with isolated maximum storm totals of 12 inches, 
across coastal portions of the Mexican states of Guerrero, 
Michoacán, Colima and Jalisco. This rainfall may produce 
life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of 
steep terrain.

For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with 
Rachel, please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall 
Graphic available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep3.shtml?rainqpf
 
SURF: Swells generated by Rachel will affect the southwestern coast
of Mexico during the next couple of days and spread northward along
the coast of west-central Mexico and the Baja California Peninsula
through the end of the week. These swells are likely to cause
life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please consult
products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 PM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Beven
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)

item.title: Hurricane Rachel Forecast Discussion Number 15
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM MST Wed Sep 30 2026 
000
WTPZ43 KNHC 302042
TCDEP3
 
Hurricane Rachel Discussion Number  15
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
200 PM MST Wed Sep 30 2026

Data from a NOAA Hurricane Hunter aircraft along with conventional 
and microwave satellite imagery shows that Rachel has been 
re-organizing for the past several hours. Microwave data near 13Z 
indicated that the cyclone had a ragged inner core with no 
organized eyewall. During the time that the aircraft has been in the 
storm, the eyewall has gotten better defined in the southeastern 
semicircle and the radius of maximum winds is getting smaller.  The 
maximum 700-mb flight-level winds reported by the aircraft has been 
82 kt, and the central pressure is currently near 978 mb.  Based 
mainly on the aircraft data, the initial intensity is held at 75 
kt. It should be noted that shear analyses show that the hurricane 
is still be affected by about 20 kt of northeasterly vertical wind 
shear.

The initial motion is still northwestward or 315/7 kt. Rachel 
continues to move along the southwestern side of a mid-tropospheric 
ridge over northern and central Mexico.  This ridge is weakening 
due to the effects of a large mid- to upper-level trough seen in 
water vapor imagery over the southwestern United States and 
northwestern Mexico.  As this trough moves northeastward and 
weakens during the next couple of days, this should allow another 
ridge to build to the north of the tropical cyclone.  As a result, 
Rachel is forecast to turn west-northwest and pass well south of 
the Baja California Peninsula before continuing westward away from 
land. The new forecast track is a little to the north of the 
previous track for the first 60 h, and thereafter is similar to the 
previous track.
 
Environmental conditions appear favorable for strengthening through 
at least 48 h, and rapid strengthening is a possibility if the 
tighter inner core that Rachel is trying to develop maintains 
itself. Thus, the early portion of the intensity forecast keeps the 
same rate of intensification to a major hurricane as the previous 
forecasts. However, there remains two possible negative influences 
including the ongoing shear and Rachel crossing a track of cooler 
water left by Polo. Later on the forecast period, decreasing sea 
surface temperatures under the forecast track and dry air 
entrainment could cause some weakening. The new intensity forecast 
is again an update of the previous forecast, and it lies near the 
upper edge of the intensity guidance.
 
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Although the core of Rachel is forecast to remain offshore of
Mexico, wind gusts of tropical-storm force are possible along 
portions of the coast of southwestern Mexico through tonight.
 
2. Outer bands from Rachel will continue to produce locally heavy 
rainfall across portions of coastal southwest Mexico. This rainfall 
may produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in 
areas of steep terrain.
 
3. Large waves could produce life-threatening surf and rip current
conditions along the southwestern and west-central coast of Mexico
and the southern Baja California Peninsula during the next several
days.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  30/2100Z 18.8N 108.0W   75 KT  85 MPH
 12H  01/0600Z 19.1N 108.6W   90 KT 105 MPH
 24H  01/1800Z 19.6N 109.2W  100 KT 115 MPH

$$

item.description:

WTPZ34 KNHC 010230
TCPEP4
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Depression Nineteen-E Advisory Number   7
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP192026
800 PM PDT Wed Sep 30 2026
 
...DEPRESSION BARELY A TROPICAL CYCLONE...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 PM PDT...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...15.2N 125.9W
ABOUT 1170 MI...1885 KM WSW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...30 MPH...45 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...ENE OR 70 DEGREES AT 14 MPH...22 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1006 MB...29.71 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 PM PDT (0300 UTC), the center of Tropical Depression
Nineteen-E was located near latitude 15.2 North, longitude 125.9
West. The depression is moving toward the east-northeast near 14 mph
(22 km/h) and an east to east-northeast motion is expected during 
the next day or so.
 
Maximum sustained winds remain near 30 mph (45 km/h) with higher 
gusts. The depression could become a remnant low on Thursday before 
dissipating Thursday night or Friday.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1006 mb (29.71 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 200 AM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Cangialosi

item.title: Tropical Depression Nineteen-E Forecast Discussion Number 7
item.description:
Issued at 800 PM PDT Wed Sep 30 2026 
146 
WTPZ44 KNHC 010231
TCDEP4
 
Tropical Depression Nineteen-E Discussion Number   7
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP192026
800 PM PDT Wed Sep 30 2026
 
Satellite images indicate that Tropical Depression Nineteen-E is
poorly organized and barely a tropical cyclone. Although the system
is producing some deep convection, it has been transient and lacks
organization. In addition, the low-level circulation is becoming
increasingly elongated from northeast to southwest. The initial
intensity is held at 25 kt, in agreement with the latest satellite
estimates.

Strong vertical wind shear and dry air should cause continued 
weakening. The system could be declared a remnant low on Thursday if 
the convection does not increase in organization. Regardless of its 
status overnight and Thursday, it seems very likely that  
the depression will dissipate in 24 to 36 hours as it approaches 
Hurricane Rachel to its east. The NHC forecast has moved up 
dissipation to 36 hours, in agreement with all of the global model 
guidance.

The depression is moving east-northeastward at 12 kt, and that 
general motion is expected to continue in the low-level flow until 
the system dissipates.
